title: AP Special TET Physical Science — Content & Pedagogy Batch 03

questions.question: The SI unit of electric potential difference is:
questions.explanation: Potential difference is measured in volts (V).

questions.question: A 9 V battery is connected across a 3 Ω resistor. Current is:
questions.explanation: Using I = V/R, current = 9/3 = 3 A.

questions.question: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are in series. Equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation: Series resistances add: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω.

questions.question: Two 4 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors in parallel, R_eq = R/2 = 2 Ω.

questions.question: Which component stores electric charge in an electric field?
questions.explanation: A capacitor stores charge and energy in an electric field.

questions.question: An electric fuse should be connected:
questions.explanation: A series fuse interrupts the circuit when excessive current flows.

questions.question: The commercial unit of electrical energy is:
questions.explanation: Electrical energy consumption is commonly billed in kilowatt-hours.

questions.question: A 500 W appliance runs for 4 hours. Energy consumed is:
questions.explanation: 0.5 kW × 4 h = 2 kWh.

questions.question: A current of 2 A flows for 5 seconds. Charge transferred is:
The resistance of an ideal ammeter is:
questions.explanation: An ammeter is designed with very low resistance to minimize circuit disturbance.

questions.question: A voltmeter is connected:
questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures potential difference across a component, so it is connected in parallel.

questions.question: The magnetic field inside a long current-carrying solenoid is approximately:
questions.explanation: A long solenoid produces an approximately uniform field inside.

questions.question: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by:
options: Removing its core in every case
questions.explanation: Increasing current generally strengthens the magnetic field of the coil.

questions.question: Electromagnetic induction occurs when:
options: Magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes
A wire is motionless in an unchanging field
A cell is disconnected from all conductors
questions.explanation: A changing magnetic flux can induce an emf in a circuit.

questions.question: The frequency of AC mains in India is:
questions.explanation: The standard mains frequency in India is 50 Hz.

questions.question: A step-up transformer has:
options: More turns in the secondary than primary
Fewer turns in the secondary than primary
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer increases voltage with a greater secondary turns count.

questions.question: A transformer cannot operate with steady DC because:
options: There is no continuously changing magnetic flux after the transient
questions.explanation: A transformer requires changing magnetic flux to induce secondary emf.

questions.question: Which electromagnetic wave has the highest frequency among these?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays occupy the high-frequency end of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.question: Which electromagnetic radiation is commonly used in medical imaging of bones?
questions.explanation: X-rays can pass through soft tissue more readily than bone, producing contrast.

questions.question: Infrared radiation is strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: Warm objects emit infrared radiation as part of their thermal radiation.

questions.question: A concave lens generally forms an image that is:
options: Virtual, erect and diminished for a real object
questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges rays and usually forms a virtual, erect, diminished image.

questions.question: An object placed at 2F of a convex lens forms an image:
questions.explanation: For an object at twice the focal length, the image forms at 2F, real, inverted and equal in size.

questions.question: The focal length of a lens is related to its power by:
questions.explanation: Lens power in dioptres is the reciprocal of focal length in metres.

questions.question: A lens of focal length +0.5 m has power:
questions.explanation: P = 1/0.5 = +2 dioptres.

questions.question: The phenomenon that explains why the sky appears blue is mainly:
questions.explanation: Shorter visible wavelengths are scattered more strongly by air molecules.

questions.question: A mirage on a hot road is associated with:
options: Refraction through layers of air and total internal reflection effects
questions.explanation: Temperature-dependent refractive-index gradients can bend light and create mirage images.

questions.question: A real image can be:
options: Seen only in a plane mirror
Formed only by a concave lens
questions.explanation: A real image is formed by actual convergence of rays and can be projected onto a screen.

questions.question: The normal to a surface at the point of incidence is:
options: A line perpendicular to the surface
A line parallel to the surface
questions.explanation: The normal is defined as perpendicular to the surface at the incidence point.

questions.question: If the angle between incident and reflected rays is 80° for a plane mirror, angle of incidence is:
questions.explanation: The two rays make equal angles with the normal, so their separation is twice incidence: 40°.

questions.question: The speed of sound in air generally increases when:
options: Air pressure is reduced at constant temperature and density effects ignored
questions.explanation: In air, sound speed increases with temperature.

questions.question: A sound wave in air is:
questions.explanation: Sound in air propagates as compressions and rarefactions, a longitudinal wave.

questions.question: The audible frequency range for a typical young human is approximately:
questions.explanation: The commonly quoted hearing range is about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.

questions.question: An instrument used to measure sound level is a:
questions.explanation: A sound level meter measures sound pressure level, usually in decibels.

questions.question: Resonance occurs when a periodic driving frequency is close to the system's:
questions.explanation: Near the natural frequency, oscillation amplitude can become large.

questions.question: A wave has a period of 0.01 s. Its frequency is:
questions.explanation: Frequency = 1/T = 1/0.01 = 100 Hz.

questions.question: The principle of a simple pendulum for small oscillations gives period proportional to:
questions.explanation: For small oscillations, T = 2π√(L/g), so T is proportional to √L.

questions.question: The amount of heat needed to raise temperature depends on:
options: Mass, specific heat capacity and temperature change
questions.explanation: For no phase change, Q = mcΔT.

questions.question: A metal spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon at the same room temperature because metal:
options: Conducts heat away from the hand faster
questions.explanation: Metal's higher thermal conductivity makes heat leave the hand more quickly.

questions.question: During boiling at constant pressure, supplied heat mainly:
options: Provides latent heat for the phase change
Changes the substance into an element
questions.explanation: At the boiling point, energy is used to convert liquid into vapour.

questions.question: The process by which a liquid changes to vapour below its boiling point is:
questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs at the surface and can happen below boiling temperature.

questions.question: Which surface is generally the best emitter and absorber of thermal radiation?
questions.explanation: Dull black surfaces are generally good absorbers and emitters of thermal radiation.

questions.question: The SI unit of specific heat capacity is:
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity is energy per unit mass per unit temperature change.

questions.question: A bimetallic strip bends on heating because its metals:
questions.explanation: Different coefficients of expansion cause the bonded strip to curve.

questions.question: Which change is endothermic?
questions.explanation: Melting requires energy input to overcome intermolecular attractions.

questions.question: The chemical symbol for potassium is:
questions.explanation: Potassium's symbol K comes from its Latin name, kalium.

questions.question: The valency of oxygen in water is commonly:
questions.explanation: Oxygen typically forms two bonds in water and has valency 2 in this context.

questions.question: A neutral atom has equal numbers of:
questions.explanation: Equal proton and electron counts give zero net charge.

questions.question: Which particle has a negative charge?
questions.explanation: An electron carries negative elementary charge.

questions.question: The mass number of an atom is the total number of:
questions.explanation: Mass number is the sum of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

questions.question: A covalent bond is formed mainly by:
questions.explanation: Covalent bonding involves sharing one or more pairs of electrons.

questions.question: An ionic bond is primarily the electrostatic attraction between:
questions.explanation: Ionic bonding arises from attraction between cations and anions.

questions.question: Which solution conducts electricity well?
questions.explanation: Dissolved sodium chloride forms mobile ions that carry charge.

questions.question: A solution is saturated at a given temperature when it:
options: Contains the maximum dissolved solute at equilibrium
questions.explanation: A saturated solution holds the maximum amount of solute under the specified conditions.

questions.question: The process of a solid forming from a solution as crystals is:
questions.explanation: Crystallization obtains a solid in crystal form from a solution or melt.

questions.question: Which metal is liquid near room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is liquid at ordinary room temperature.

questions.question: Which metal is commonly stored under kerosene to limit reaction with air and moisture?
questions.explanation: Highly reactive sodium is stored under kerosene or a suitable protective liquid.

questions.question: The major ore of aluminium is:
questions.explanation: Bauxite is the principal commercial ore of aluminium.

questions.question: Galvanization protects iron by coating it with:
questions.explanation: A zinc coating protects iron from corrosion.

questions.question: The gas evolved at the cathode during electrolysis of acidified water is:
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is produced at the cathode; oxygen forms at the anode.

questions.question: The electrolyte in a lead-acid car battery contains:
questions.explanation: A lead-acid battery uses aqueous sulphuric acid as its electrolyte.

questions.question: Which is a strong acid among these?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid ionizes essentially completely in dilute aqueous solution.

questions.question: A base that dissolves in water is called an:
questions.explanation: An alkali is a water-soluble base.

questions.question: The reaction between zinc and dilute hydrochloric acid produces:
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

questions.question: Which gas is a common product of thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate?
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ decomposes on heating to calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: The formula of washing soda is commonly written as:
questions.explanation: Washing soda is hydrated sodium carbonate, usually Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.question: The formula of plaster of Paris is:
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate.

questions.question: Which process is used to obtain oxygen and nitrogen from air industrially?
questions.explanation: Air is liquefied and separated into components by fractional distillation.

questions.question: The main constituent of biogas is:
questions.explanation: Biogas is methane-rich, with carbon dioxide and other gases also present.

questions.question: Which fuel is often described as a cleaner fossil fuel because it emits less particulate matter and sulphur dioxide than coal when burned?
questions.explanation: Natural gas generally burns with fewer particulates and less SO₂ than coal, though it still emits CO₂.

questions.question: The conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into usable nitrogen compounds by certain microbes is:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing microorganisms convert N₂ into biologically usable nitrogen compounds.

questions.question: Which pollutant is strongly associated with acid rain formation?
questions.explanation: SO₂ and nitrogen oxides can form acids in the atmosphere.

questions.question: The ozone layer is located mainly in the:
questions.explanation: Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere.

questions.question: Which action directly helps reduce household electricity use?
options: Use efficient appliances and switch off unused devices
Keep lights on in empty rooms
questions.explanation: Efficient devices and avoiding unnecessary use reduce electricity consumption.

questions.question: A teacher wants to introduce the idea of inertia. Which demonstration is most suitable?
options: Quickly pull a card from under a coin and observe the coin's motion
Measure the pH of lemon juice
questions.explanation: The coin tends to remain at rest as the card is pulled rapidly.

questions.question: When teaching pressure, a useful comparison is to press a blunt and sharp object with:
options: Similar force and compare the contact area and effect
questions.explanation: Holding force approximately constant helps illustrate how area affects pressure.

questions.question: Which prompt most directly checks whether students understand the difference between mass and weight?
options: How would the same object’s mass and weight compare on Earth and the Moon, and why?
questions.explanation: The question asks learners to apply the distinction between intrinsic mass and gravitational force.

questions.question: In a practical investigation, why should students record observations promptly?
options: To reduce reliance on memory and preserve a clear evidence record
To make the result match the prediction
questions.explanation: Prompt records help maintain accuracy and traceability of observations.

questions.question: Which teacher question encourages evidence-based explanation?
options: Can you repeat the sentence exactly?
questions.explanation: Asking for supporting observations connects claims to evidence.

questions.question: A student says that a heavier object must have greater density. The teacher should guide them to compare:
options: Mass and volume together for each object
questions.explanation: Density depends on the ratio of mass to volume, not mass alone.

questions.question: A class compares insulation materials. The dependent variable might be:
options: The measured temperature change over a fixed interval
The type of material deliberately selected
questions.explanation: Temperature change is the measured outcome; material type is the manipulated factor.

questions.question: Which classroom assessment is best for checking safe laboratory technique?
options: A practical observation checklist during an activity
A final score with no observation
questions.explanation: A checklist can document whether learners demonstrate safe procedures.

questions.question: A teacher uses a simulation to teach atomic structure. Learners should also be reminded that:
options: The simulation is a simplified representation of atoms
The colours and sizes shown must be literal
questions.explanation: Models simplify reality and should be interpreted with their limitations in mind.

questions.question: Which activity is most appropriate for developing science process skills?
options: Plan a test, identify variables, take measurements and interpret results
questions.explanation: The task exercises planning, variable control, measurement and interpretation.

questions.question: When a learner's result differs from the class pattern, the teacher should:
options: Check the procedure and data with the learner before drawing conclusions
Tell the learner to alter the numbers
questions.explanation: Checking method and records first supports fair, evidence-based evaluation.

questions.question: A learner can state Ohm's law but cannot use it in a circuit problem. The teacher should provide:
options: Guided practice interpreting voltage, current and resistance in varied circuits
More copying of the sentence only
questions.explanation: Application practice connects the relationship to quantities and circuit contexts.

questions.question: Which strategy supports learners with different language proficiencies in science?
options: Use labelled visuals, vocabulary supports and opportunities to explain ideas in varied ways
Assess language accent rather than science understanding
questions.explanation: Visual and language scaffolds can make scientific concepts more accessible.

questions.question: Why should a teacher ask students to critique a scientific claim found online?
options: To practise checking evidence, reasoning and source credibility
To teach that every online claim is true
questions.explanation: Evaluating claims and sources is part of scientific literacy.

questions.question: A student draws a graph with axes but no units. The teacher should explain that units:
options: Clarify the scale and meaning of the measured quantities
questions.explanation: Units are necessary for interpreting numerical measurements correctly.

questions.question: Which is a sound reason to use local examples when teaching energy resources?
options: They help connect scientific ideas to learners' lived context and decisions
They prove local practice is always scientifically correct
They remove the need for evidence
questions.explanation: Local examples can contextualize concepts while still requiring evidence and analysis.

questions.question: A teacher asks students to compare the advantages and limitations of solar and wind energy. This mainly develops:
questions.explanation: Comparing trade-offs requires using criteria and supporting judgments with reasons.

questions.question: Which action demonstrates responsible scientific data handling?
options: Record measurements honestly, including unexpected results
Change values to fit a predicted outcome
questions.explanation: Honest recording preserves the integrity of scientific investigation.

questions.question: A teacher notices repeated confusion between current and voltage. A useful response is to:
options: Use a circuit model and measurements to contrast charge flow with potential difference
Ask students to memorize both words without meaning
questions.explanation: Models and measurements can clarify that current and voltage represent different quantities.

questions.question: Which learning objective is most observable and assessable?
options: Students will draw a labelled field pattern around a bar magnet and describe it
questions.explanation: The objective specifies visible work and an explanation that can be assessed.

questions.question: A teacher invites students to propose more than one method for separating a mixture. This encourages:
options: Flexible problem solving and justification of method choice
questions.explanation: Considering alternatives and justifying choices develops reasoning about properties.

questions.question: Which prompt best supports reflection after a practical task?
options: What would you change next time, and what evidence leads you to that choice?
Can you copy the aim again?
questions.explanation: The prompt asks learners to use experience and evidence to plan improvement.

questions.question: A student concludes that a plant grew taller because of fertilizer after testing only one plant. The teacher should point out the need for:
options: More observations and a suitable comparison/control
questions.explanation: A comparison and replication help evaluate alternative explanations and variation.

questions.question: Which statement best describes science as a way of knowing?
options: Explanations are developed and revised in light of observations and evidence
Authority alone makes a claim true
questions.explanation: Scientific knowledge is evidence-based and open to refinement as evidence develops.

questions.question: A teacher provides immediate feedback during circuit construction. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Feedback during learning helps learners correct and improve performance.

questions.question: Which task best assesses learners' ability to communicate a scientific investigation?
options: Present a question, method, data, conclusion and evidence-based limitations
questions.explanation: A structured report communicates the investigation and its evidential basis.

questions.question: Which is the best response if an experiment involves a hazardous material unsuitable for learners?
options: Use a safer alternative, teacher demonstration or suitable simulation with risk controls
Ask learners to smell it closely
questions.explanation: Risk assessment and safer substitutions protect learners while preserving learning goals.
